topic: 450 XC-F 2017 weight, range, speed and engine feel
statement: A 2017 450 XC-F weighed 241 lb with a full 2.2-gallon tank and 230 lb without fuel, and listed at $10,099. It goes about 50 miles on a tank and runs into the limiter at 91 mph on stock gearing. The engine is torque-heavy and hooks up, and still revs freely on top. It stalls easily at small throttle openings if the clutch work is sloppy.

topic: 450 XC-F 2017 map switch and traction control
statement: The 2017 450 XC-F's bar switch gives four settings: two maps, each with traction control on or off, changeable while riding. The aggressive map suits good traction. The milder map with traction control on is easier when the throttle is opened fast, and traction control helps most for riders who spin the tyre or on loose ground.

On the 2017 450 XC-F the air fork has more small-bump compliance than the 2016 4CS. Testers added 1 psi and a few clicks of fork compression for balance, added up to five clicks of shock low-speed compression for the motocross track, and ran 103-108 mm of rider sag.

vals.fork: +1 psi, a few clicks more compression

statement: The 2017 450 XC-F has a close-ratio five-speed. Stock gearing tops out at 91 mph, and testers recommended re-gearing either way for tight trails or for fast desert, and wished for a sixth gear or wider spacing.

Findings on a 2017 450 XC-F: it stalls unless the idle is set properly; slipping the clutch heats the engine and the clutch damping rubbers should be checked every 20 hours; the exhaust is loud for off-road use; there is no skid plate and the handguards are light; the lithium battery needs warming before it cranks well in cold weather; and the push-button fuel cap is stiff when cold.

topic: 250 XC-F 2015 weight, range, speed and engine feel
statement: A 2015 250 XC-F weighed 247 lb with a full 2.4-gallon tank (about 15 lb less empty) and listed at $8,599. It went nearly 70 miles on a tank at a conservative trail pace, or about an hour at race pace, and ran 89-90 mph (98.1 with a tailwind). The power is long, smooth and linear and builds with revs to nearly 14,000 rpm. The flywheel effect is light, so stalls come suddenly.

The 2015 250 XC-F has the same engine and chassis as the 250 SX-F, with only a side-stand tab added to the frame. It adds a larger tank, the side stand, an 18-inch rear wheel, handguards and off-road suspension valving, on a six-speed semi-wide-ratio gearbox. The engine has a plain big-end bearing.

On the 2015 250 XC-F the 4CS fork's adjuster works mainly on mid-speed damping and needs 3-5 clicks before a change is felt, while 1-2 clicks on the shock are noticeable. For motocross, run it stock (riders under 165 lb may want softer springs). For off-road, go 3-5 clicks softer on fork compression and rebound, match the shock softer and take half a turn off the shock's high-speed compression. Sag is 100-105 mm. For tight racing add two rear teeth or drop one on the countershaft.

Findings on a 2015 250 XC-F: fork stiction on hard ground (oiling the seals and bleeding the air helped), a stock rear tyre that struggles on hard surfaces, fragile handguards that discolour, a touchy rear brake, no skid plate, and a loud muffler with no spark arrestor.
The oil tank on the 2018 injected TE 300 could leak. Testers reported it fixed for 2019.

source.name: Motocross Action - 2019 Husqvarna TE300i race test

statement: Of the 2016 two-strokes, the TE 250 is the livelier, with smooth, predictable power, less vibration and a lighter feel. The TE 300 pulls harder from the bottom and needs less clutch in slow going. Both feel planted and are less likely to deflect off roots and rocks than the 125. Both have a two-map switch on the bar.

topic: FE 350, FE 450 and FE 501 ride character (2016)
statement: Of the 2016 FE four-strokes, the 350 is very usable and can be revved or lugged, though its weight shows when changing direction or slowing. The 450 has strong, usable power and finds traction well in tight going, with suspension that works best when pushed, but it is a lot of bike for a full day. The 501 is extremely powerful and limited by grip off-road: it is best left in third gear with a finger on the clutch, feels heavy in tight terrain, and an auto-clutch was suggested for it.

The street-legal 2016 FE 501 weighs 250 lb without fuel, holds 2.4 gallons and listed at $10,599. It has a heavier crankshaft than the off-road FE 501, 11.8:1 compression, a 42 mm throttle body and a quiet exhaust, with tall road gearing (first is good for over 30 mph). It has tractable torque at any speed and the suspension takes hard hits well. The front end feels light with no steering damper, the stock rims are unbalanced and bounce at highway speed, the tank is small for long rides and no handguards are fitted.
notes: Source tested the street-legal S version.

source.name: Ultimate Motorcycling - 2016 Husqvarna FE 501 S test

statement: On the 2017 TE 250 and TE 300 the stock suspension is soft and at times short of control for a rider over about 90 kg. Gearing felt tall for tight going; two or three more teeth on the rear were suggested. The 300 is strong, linear and nearly vibration-free but snappy in the upper midrange when the rider is tired, and the 250 is more controllable and less tiring. Three power-valve springs are supplied for tuning the hit. Dry weights are 102.2 kg (250) and 102.4 kg (300).

vals.gearing: +2 or 3 rear teeth for tight terrain

source.name: BikeReview - 2017 Husqvarna TE 250 and TE 300 review

statement: In competition tune a 2018 FE 350 made 48 PS at 10,000 rpm and 39.7 Nm at 7,900 rpm on a magazine dyno, and weighed 114 kg with a full 8.5-litre tank. The bar switch changes throttle response between two settings and traction control can be switched on or off. The suspension responds well over bumps and has reserve for big jumps.

In 2019 the FX 350 is a hybrid of motocross and enduro parts: about 6 kg lighter than the FE 350, with the WP AER 48 air fork and the 2019 motocross-range engine and chassis upgrades the FE did not yet have. The FE 350 has a sharp-steering chassis with forgiving power and suspension that suit tight, slippery terrain.

The 2016 450 XC-F took the new, smaller and lighter chassis and engine at the same time as the 450 SX-F and performs identically on power: smooth, torquey, able to chug at low revs and pull away on the throttle. Its off-road valving has less high-speed compression and rebound damping than the SX-F, so it is plusher without wallowing, the 4CS fork is less harsh at the top of the stroke than earlier versions, and it still copes with a motocross track. A rubber-mounted bar cuts vibration. It is a lot of bike in tight woods, resists turning more than the 350 XC-F, and suits open terrain, desert and GP-style racing.

source.name: Dirt Bike Test - 2016 KTM 450XC-F riding impression

statement: The 2016 XC-F models share frame, engine and mapping with the SX-F motocross bikes and add an 18-inch rear wheel, handguards, off-road suspension settings, a 2.25-gallon tank (1.85 on the SX-F) and a side stand. The 250 XC-F gained torque and bottom-end with a smoother move into the midrange and is strong on tight, technical ground. The 350 XC-F has a wide powerband with a strong bottom but needs more shifting on a track. The 450 XC-F has heavy bottom-end torque and is best ridden a gear higher than usual; ridden like a motocross bike it wears the rider out.

source.name: Cycle News - 2016 KTM SX-F and XC-F first rides

statement: For 2013 the 500 XC-W got new fork oil for more consistent damping, a rear brake master cylinder with less seal wear, and black-coated spokes on new rims. It is a 510.4 cc (95 x 72 mm) four-stroke with a hydraulic clutch, a 48 mm WP open-cartridge fork (300 mm travel) and a PDS shock (335 mm), 13/50 gearing, a 2.25-gallon tank and a 970 mm seat, and weighs about 247 lb without fuel. US list price $9,649.
For 2015 the 500 XC-W got a lighter DDS clutch basket and new O-rings on the oil-pump suction screen for durability.

source.name: Off-Road.com - 2015 KTM dual-sport and cross-country bikes

topic: FX 350 and FX 450 2019 engine and chassis changes
statement: For 2019 the FX 350 and FX 450 got a stiffer frame and triple clamps, a two-piece subframe about 9 oz lighter, new damping in the AER 48 fork and a shock with a new main piston, radiators mounted nearly half an inch lower, slimmer bodywork, new header pipes with a resonance chamber that come off without disturbing the shock, a shorter muffler, new launch and traction control settings and skid-plate mounts. The FX 450 got a lower cylinder head nearly 18 oz lighter with a new camshaft. The FX 350 got a head 7 oz lighter, larger titanium valves and a diaphragm-spring steel clutch that saves nearly 7 oz; it revs to 13,400 rpm.

source.name: Ultimate Motorcycling - 2019 Husqvarna cross country line-up first look

topic: FX 350 2018 map switch, traction control and launch control
statement: The 2018 FX 350's bar switch chooses between two maps, turns traction control on or off and arms launch control for starts. Traction control compares throttle position with how fast the revs are rising and trims power when they climb too quickly. The bike is a 349.7 cc DOHC six-speed (semi-close ratios) with a Magura hydraulic clutch, the WP AER 48 fork (310 mm travel), a linkage shock (300 mm), a 2.25-gallon tank and a 960 mm seat, and weighs 221.8 lb without fuel.
